contract: The solver builds a scheduler for immutable DAGs of at most 32 nodes. Workers claim ready nodes under 10-unit leases with increasing fencing tokens, and each execution has its own logical clock. Claim IDs are idempotent, expired leases can be reclaimed, and only the current unexpired lease holder can complete a node.

study.title: Distributed Job Scheduler
study.reason: The case study's dependency handling, claim and lease lifecycle, and stale-worker fencing map directly onto the claim, advance and complete operations.

pstates.name: $$executions
pstates.key: execution id; claims keyed by claim id

topologies.name: lifecycle
topologies.does: validates DAGs, advances the clock, decides claims and records completions

design.ownership: Every event and all state for one execution live on the execution id's partition, so claim and completion decisions are local and need no hops. Reads are direct point selects on $$executions; there is no query topology.

stated: Work may scale with the one DAG, not with other executions, claims or workers
Reads of one execution must not touch another execution's state
State is durable and the module runs on 2 and 4 tasks
Writes to one execution apply in invocation order
Claim IDs are idempotent; external effects need not be exactly once

tested.nfr: Cost independent of other executions and same-execution denials
tested.mechanism: Event hook sums reads, iterators, iterator reads and commit batches for 8 probes at 256 and 1024; bound is max(12, 8 + 3 x before)
Re-reads state after update-module
Runs on 2 and 4 tasks with two clients
Replays a claim ID with different arguments and checks the first decision stands

gaps.gap: Growth probes cover only no-op and denial paths
gaps.wrongDesign: An effective clock advance, grant or completion scans the execution's whole claim history to find expired leases or recount attempts
A stream topology writes the node lease, then the claim decision; a retry between them re-decides as lease-held and strands token N

gaps.gap: Blob storage is invisible to operation counts
gaps.wrongDesign: Claims kept as one non-subindexed map per execution; each claim rewrites the whole map in one write

contract: The solver builds the durable core of a push notification platform. It keeps a per-recipient device registry with token generations and per-category preferences. Idempotent submissions fan out to devices, delivery attempts are guarded with bounded retries, permanent failures go to a dead-letter record, and client receipts only move forward.

study.title: Notification System
study.reason: The case study's device token handling, user preferences and retry-with-dead-letter delivery pipeline map directly onto the submit, attempt and receipt operations.

pstates.name: $$users
pstates.schema: {String {:profile {devices, prefs, submit-seq}, :recent {Long String} subindexed, :dead-letters {Long record} subindexed}}

topologies.name: core
topologies.does: arbitrates first-wins submissions, tracks deliveries, retries and dead letters

design.ownership: Events hash by owner. Submissions are arbitrated per submission id within the batch using per-task position ranks, then stored by submission id. Delivery effects use |hash back to the user's partition to update recent history, dead letters and device state.

stated: Submit is fixed work, bounded by 8 devices and independent of history
Attempts, receipts and point reads are fixed; pages are bounded by 100 entries
Work and storage are balanced across tasks
Workload of up to 100,000 submissions and dead letters per recipient
Latency figures are explicitly not thresholds

tested.nfr: Point, page, submit, attempt and receipt cost independent of history
tested.mechanism: Event hook counts reads, iterators and commit batches at 240 and 1040 history on one 8-device user; bound is small + 150 per metric
Asserts the measured totals are positive
Re-reads next-attempt time and attempt count after update-module
Each test runs on 2 and 4 tasks with a second client
Replays submissions and sends stale reports, then checks state is unchanged

gaps.wrongDesign: Every submit routes through |global to a single seen-submissions set before hashing by user

gaps.gap: Blob storage of per-user history passes
gaps.wrongDesign: Recent submissions kept as a plain growing vector; each submit rewrites it in one write

gaps.gap: No retry injection for dead letters
gaps.wrongDesign: A stream topology marks the delivery failed, then appends the dead letter on the user partition; a retry drops or duplicates the entry

contract: The solver builds the durable core of a crawl frontier. It deduplicates URLs exactly under a restricted HTTPS canonicalization and keeps per-host queues in lexicographic order. It applies caller-configured robots rules and a per-host politeness delay, and grants single leases with fencing tokens so stale workers cannot release newer or expired leases.

study.title: Web Crawler
study.reason: The case study's URL frontier, host politeness and deduplication sections map directly onto the discover, claim and complete operations.

pstates.name: $$hosts
pstates.schema: {String {:info {delay, rules, lease, queued counter}, :urls {String status} subindexed, :pending #{String} subindexed, :claims {String decision} subindexed}}

topologies.name: core
topologies.does: orders each host's commands and updates URLs, the pending queue, leases and claims

design.ownership: All state for a host lives on the host's partition, so dedup, politeness and fencing are local decisions. A very hot host concentrates on one task. Reads are direct selects on $$hosts; there is no query topology.

stated: Discover is fixed work per URL, independent of queue size
Claim is fixed plus amortized per blocked URL and must not scan the queue
Complete and point reads are fixed; the queued count must not come from scanning
List-pending is bounded by its limit; work is balanced across tasks
Workload of up to 1 million pending URLs per host

tested.nfr: Claim cost independent of retired URLs, claim history and queue size
tested.mechanism: Sums reads, iterators, iterator reads and topology select and transform counts at small and large populations; bound is small + 100
Same counter at limits 1, 20 and 100
Checks correctness; cost is only checked to be positive
Re-reads state after update-module
Runs on 2 and 4 tasks with a second client

gaps.gap: Discover, complete and get-host costs are never measured
gaps.wrongDesign: Each discover or get-host counts the whole pending set to compute the queued number
Each claim rewrites every blocked URL's status record or re-persists the pending set
Pending URLs kept as one non-subindexed sorted set per host; each discover rewrites up to 1 million entries

contract: The solver builds a multi-tenant feature flag store. Each flag holds one whole configuration, and a write replaces it only when its revision is strictly newer. Evaluation applies a kill switch, ordered equality rules, a SHA-256 percentage rollout and then the default, and bucketing is deterministic and reads no stored state.

study.title: Feature Flag Service
study.reason: The case study's deterministic targeting, configuration versioning and kill switch map directly onto the put, evaluate and compute-bucket operations.

pstates.name: $$flags
pstates.schema: {FlagId {revision, kill switch, off and default values, ordered rules, optional rollout}}

topologies.name: flags
topologies.does: replaces a flag's configuration when the revision is newer

design.ownership: Each flag is owned by the partition of its FlagId, so revision checks are local and there are no hops. Evaluation is a direct point read of one flag followed by client-side logic; bucketing is a pure client computation.

stated: Evaluate and get read only the one flag's configuration
Work must not grow with the number of flags, environments or tenants
Put is proportional to its supplied configuration
Compute-bucket must not read stored state
Writes to one flag keep order; state is durable on 2 and 4 tasks

tested.nfr: Get, evaluate and put cost independent of unrelated flags
tested.mechanism: Event hook counts reads and writes at 240 and 1,240 flags across 17 tenants and 11 environments; bound is 12 + 3 x small
Asserts zero reads and zero writes while computing a bucket
Re-reads configuration after update-module
Sends equal revisions in one unsynchronized group and checks the first wins

gaps.gap: Unrelated flags sit in other environments
gaps.wrongDesign: Evaluate scans a per-environment map of flags and filters by key; each environment holds only about 7 flags, so growth stays under the bound
One configuration bundle per [tenant env], read and rewritten whole on every get and put

gaps.gap: Task balance is not stated or tested
gaps.wrongDesign: Every flag write hashes to one constant key or goes through |global

contract: The solver builds the retrieval and authorization core of a multi-tenant RAG platform. Document content has monotonic revisions and tombstones, while document ACLs and user group memberships have their own independent revisions. A keyword query scores chunks by distinct token overlap and authorizes every candidate before ranking and truncating to top k.

study.title: Enterprise RAG System
study.reason: The case study's tenant and ACL-aware retrieval and document freshness concerns map directly onto revisioned documents, ACLs, memberships and the authorized query.

depots.name: *writes
depots.partition: hash by :key (DocKey [tenant doc-id] or UserKey [tenant user-id])

topologies.name: entities
topologies.does: applies revisioned content, ACL and membership writes and diffs token postings

design.ownership: Document and user writes land on their key's partition. Content changes diff old and new chunks and use |hash by token key to update postings. Queries run in the client: one select per query token, then one per candidate document, with authorization before top k.

stated: Query must not scan chunks without a query token or read another tenant's data
Put and delete are proportional to one document's chunks
ACL and membership writes must not do document- or chunk-proportional work
Gets read one entity
Authorization happens before top-k truncation

tested.nfr: Query cost independent of unrelated documents
tested.mechanism: Counts RocksDB reads at 256 and 2,048 documents, half in another tenant containing the query token; bound is small + 16

tested.nfr: Query cost independent of non-matching chunks
tested.mechanism: Adds 31 non-matching chunks to the matching document under the same bound

tested.nfr: ACL write cost independent of corpus and chunk count
tested.mechanism: Counts reads and writes for an ACL change at both corpus sizes
Re-reads state after update-module
Uses the same IDs in two tenants and checks results stay separate

gaps.gap: Membership write cost is never measured
gaps.wrongDesign: A per-user eligible-chunk index rebuilt by scanning the tenant's documents on each group change

gaps.gap: Put and delete costs are never measured
gaps.wrongDesign: Each token's posting list is a non-subindexed set, read and rewritten whole on every put

gaps.gap: No retry injection for posting maintenance
gaps.wrongDesign: A stream topology stores the content revision first; on retry the revision guard skips, so postings are never written or removed
